definitions.explanation: A story that is invented or made up rather than based on fact. Often carries a negative nuance suggesting deception or lying.

examples.japanese: それは{作|つく}り{話|ばなし}だろう。
examples.english: That's a made-up story, isn't it.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{作|つく}り{話|ばなし}をしているのはすぐわかった。
examples.english: I could tell right away that the child was making up a story.

examples.japanese: あの{噂|うわさ}は{全|すべ}て{作|つく}り{話|ばなし}だったことが{後|あと}で{判明|はんめい}した。
examples.english: It was later revealed that all those rumors were fabricated stories.

notes:
Compound of {作|つく}る (to make) + {話|はなし} (story), with rendaku changing はなし to ばなし. Usually implies the story is meant to deceive, unlike {物語|ものがたり} (tale, narrative) or フィクション (fiction), which are neutral terms for creative works.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{作|つく}り{話|ばなし}をする (make up a story, tell a lie)
・{全|まった}くの{作|つく}り{話|ばなし} (a complete fabrication)
・{作|つく}り{話|ばなし}だと{見抜|みぬ}く (see through a made-up story)
